subject: NovaPay: Implementation readiness and technical handoff
messages:
From: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwoodinference.com>
To: Elena Martinez <elena.martinez@novapay.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Wed, 28 Apr 2027 15:05:00 -0700
Subject: NovaPay: Implementation readiness and technical handoff

Hi Elena —

Thanks again for the time today. Quick recap from our discovery so we have a shared implementation checklist and can scope the technical handoff:

High-level goals
- Bring real-time payment reconciliation features (batching + streaming embedders for fuzzy match) into NovaPay's reconciliation pipeline.
- Keep median latency under 250ms for line-item enrichment calls; prioritize correctness for regulatory fields.

Integration / architecture notes (from today's call)
- SDK: You prefer server-side SDK (Node + Python) with our REST fallback. Primary path: REST over TLS for initial rollout, then gRPC for heavy throughput on Dedicated.
- Auth: OIDC + short-lived tokens (client_credential flow) and optional per-tenant KMS integration for key wrapping. Need to confirm whether NovaPay will manage keys (HSM) or have Redwood KMS escrow.
- Routing: Route low-latency requests to regional Hosted nodes (us-west) and burst to Dedicated during EOD spikes. We recommended enabling per-route cost tiering so high-cardinality enrichment can fall back to cheaper quantized variants.
- Structured output & tool calling: We propose using Redwood's schema enforcement for structured outputs (JSON schema + validation hook) and tool-calling for lookups (account-verification API).
- Embeddings & reranker: Keep embeddings in region (US) and use a two-stage flow: candidate retrieval via dense embeddings, rerank with a supervised scoring head. We discussed retention window and encryption-at-rest.

Prompt templates & system prompt governance (initial proposal)
- Versioning: store prompt templates in a git repo with semver tags (prompt v1.2.0), tie versions to model rollouts.
- Injection mitigations: apply input sanitization, strict output schema validation, and a runtime prompt-safety filter that strips or signals suspicious tokens.
- Red-teaming: schedule an internal red-team run during POC (we suggested 2-week sprint with focused adversarial cases) and tie any regressions to rollback tags.

Action items (next 7 days)
- Elena: confirm whether NovaPay will provide tenant-level KMS (yes/no) and the procurement contact for SOW.
- Sanjay / procurement: request SOW review and redlines (cc'd work to come).
- Redwood (Marissa): prepare SOW v1 and a simple network diagram + security appendix.
- Redwood (Rishi): draft SDK quickstart (Node + Python) and an auth sample for OIDC client credentials.

Attachments: \"novapay-sow-v1.pdf\" (draft SOW), \"novapay-network-diagram.png\" (sketch we drew on call).

Proposed tech-handoff slots next week: Thu 10:00–11:00 PT or Fri 13:00–14:00 PT. Which works for your engineering lead?

I'll follow up internally to allocate owners and timelines.

Thanks,
Aditya
Aditya Rao
Enterprise Sales | Redwood Inference

Date: Wed, 28 Apr 2027 18:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: NovaPay: Implementation readiness and technical handoff

Thanks Aditya — this is really helpful. A couple quick clarifications before we schedule: 

1) Embeddings storage: will embeddings be stored in our project space (we want to keep them in our VPC) or in Redwood's managed store? If in Redwood's store, can we enforce per-tenant encryption keys?

2) Latency and batching: you mentioned a two-stage retrieval + rerank. For reconciliation at EOD we plan to send large batches (50–100K keys). Is that supported via your Dedicated capacity batching or do we need an offline flow?

3) Prompt governance: the red-team cadence sounds good — can you share a short checklist of what you test (prompt injection, hallucination rate thresholds, schema bypass)? We have compliance auditors who will want to see that.

Procurement: looping in Sanjay (cc) — he'll handle SOW review and redlines.

Elena
Elena Martinez
Head of Product, NovaPay

Subject: Fwd: NovaPay: Implementation readiness and technical handoff (internal)

Internal note — next steps and owners after Elena's questions. Keep concise.

Marissa / Rishi,

Elena asked three items we need to answer before scheduling the handoff. Proposed split:
- Marissa: finalize SOW (we need a short security appendix that states where embeddings will live, retention policy, and KMS options). Attach our \"redwood-prompt-versioning-guidelines.pdf\" as part of the appendix.
- Rishi: produce the SDK quickstart + auth sample and a note on batch/throughput options (Dedicated vs offline). Include an example gRPC client and a curl REST fallback.

Technical notes you can reuse for responses:
- Embeddings: we support both managed store (Redwood-managed encrypted blobstore) and self-hosted (VPC attachments). Per-tenant KMS allowed — we wrap embeddings with tenant key if they bring KMS.
- Batching: Dedicated supports large, controlled batches; for extremely large nightly jobs we recommend an async bulk ingest path (S3 -> bulk ingest job -> index build) to avoid per-request throttling. We'll document BQ/CSV examples for their EOD use case.
- Prompt governance checklist (high-level to share with compliance):
  * Prompt template repo (git) with PR review + semantic version tags.
  * Output schema enforcement with runtime validation; fail-open only with explicit overrides.
  * Input sanitization layer (strip non-UTF8, remove control characters, canonicalize user prompts).
  * Prompt-safety detector (heuristics + ML classifier) to flag injection attempts.
  * Red-team results tracked as issues; regressions tied to prompt rollback tags.

Can you both draft one-page answers we can send Elena tomorrow morning? I'll include the attachments and a proposed DocuSign SOW link.

Thanks,
Aditya

From: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwoodinference.com>

Date: Thu, 29 Apr 2027 09:40:00 -0700
Subject: Re: NovaPay: Implementation readiness and technical handoff

Elena —

Thanks for the quick follow-up. Answers below and next steps.

1) Embeddings storage: you can choose either — we support:
   - Redwood-managed encrypted store (default). Data-at-rest encrypted with Redwood KMS; tenant-level wrapping available on request.
   - VPC-attached store: embeddings remain in your VPC/storage; we only send ephemeral retrieval tokens. If you want per-tenant HSM key control, select VPC-attached + bring-your-KMS.

2) Large-batch reconciliation (50–100K keys):
   - Short answer: supported. Paths:
     * Dedicated mode: continuous batching and a controlled throughput window; good for near-real-time EOD jobs if you accept slightly higher cost.
     * Bulk ingest path (recommended for very large nightly runs): S3 -> bulk ingest job -> index build. This avoids per-request throttling and is more cost-effective for large-scale runs. We'll include an example CSV import + CLI command in the SDK docs.

3) Prompt governance checklist (summary for compliance):
   - Prompt templates in git with semver and PR review.
   - Schema-first outputs: all structured outputs validated at runtime; any schema mismatch generates an error and an audit event.
   - Injection mitigations: input sanitization, remove embedded control sequences, context-window clipping, and a prompt-safety detector that flags anomalies.
   - Red-team plan: two-week adversarial sprint during POC with prioritized testcases (injection, data exfiltration attempts, schema bypass). Results are tracked in our internal tracker; critical regressions require a prompt rollback and deploy freeze.

Attachments: SOW draft attached; network diagram; prompt versioning guidelines. DocuSign link for SOW: https://www.docusign.com/--/novapay/sow-signature. HubSpot deal: https://hubspot.redwood.company/deal/DEAL-2027-0428-NOVAPAY.

Proposed handoff: Thu May 6, 2027 10:00–11:00 PT (60m) — tech deep-dive with eng + security. Please confirm availability for your engineering lead and procurement.

Happy to hop on a quick call if you want us to walk step-by-step through the SDK sample.

Best,
Aditya
Aditya Rao
Enterprise Sales | Redwood Inference
